name: preserve-project-style
description: An existing repository convention wins over the skill default
trap: The model mechanically renames ReadPacket and m_socket to the skill's default scheme, creating a mixed-style patch instead of preserving the repository convention.
criteria: Does not request renaming identifiers that match the surrounding project
States that established repository style takes precedence
Keeps any review comments focused on concrete defects rather than personal preference

name: auto-preserves-information
description: auto is used for repetition but not where width or conversion matters
trap: The model either removes every auto mechanically or replaces every type with auto, hiding integer division and the required timeout width.
criteria: Keeps or recommends auto for make_unique and the verbose iterator case
Makes the intended type or conversion of timeout and ratio explicit
Does not introduce C++20 ranges or views under the C++17 baseline

name: self-contained-header
description: A header includes what it uses and does not leak namespace directives
trap: The model leaves transitive includes or using namespace std in the public header, so consumers compile only in a lucky include order and inherit polluted lookup.
criteria: Adds direct standard-library includes for optional, string, and string_view
Removes using namespace std from the header
Does not move ownership or API redesign into this style-only fix

name: clang-tidy-cpp17-boundary
description: Tooling enables useful families without rewriting into C++20
prompt: Create a starter .clang-tidy for a new C++17 service. I want bugprone, cppcoreguidelines and modernize checks, but CI must reject suggestions that require C++20 or C++23.
trap: The model enables modernize-* wholesale and lets fixes introduce constraints, ranges, designated initializers, starts_with, std::format, std::numbers or std::print.
criteria: Explicitly disables modernize checks that produce C++20 or C++23 constructs
Explains that clang-tidy reads -std=c++17 from the compilation database
Avoids treating warnings in third-party code as project errors
